column1: THE LETTER AND WHAT IT IS — MC 216 page 1

column4: What is this form?/ What does this packet contain
column5: What's this paper? · I got something in the mail · What is this about?
column6: It's your yearly Medi-Cal renewal. Once a year the county checks that your information is still right so your coverage keeps going. Most of it is already filled in for you.
column9: Leads with reassurance that it is pre-filled. That single fact reduces refusal more than anything else.

column4: Do I have to do this?
column5: Can I ignore it? · What if I don't send it?
column6: You do need to send it back. If you don't, your Medi-Cal can stop. I can help you get it done today.
column9: The form itself says 'You may lose your Medi-Cal if you do not respond by' the due date. Do not soften it and do not dramatise.

column4: Why is only part of my family on this form?
column5: My husband isn't on here · Where are my kids?
column6: That's normal. Anyone in your household who isn't on this form gets their own separate letter about their Medi-Cal.
column9: Stated verbatim on the form. One household can be renewing on more than one form, and on different form types.

column4: I never got the form.
column5: Nothing came in the mail · I didn't get anything
column6: That happens a lot, usually because the county has an older address. Let's get that fixed and get you a new copy.
column9: Do not treat this as a dead end — it is the highest-value correction available. Route to counsellor for the county address update.

column4: I got the form but lost it
column5: I kept it safe but seems to have lost it
column6: That happens, Let's get that fixed and get you a new copy.
column9: Do not treat this as a dead end — it is the highest-value correction available. Route to counsellor for the county address update.

column4: I already sent it.
column5: I mailed it last week · My daughter did it online
column6: Good. Let me check what the county has on file, because sometimes they come back asking for one more thing.
column9: Never close on self-reported submission. The form's own privacy section says the county will contact them if something […] [cut off in photo]

column4: It's not in my language.
column5: I can't read this · It's in English
column6: You can get this form in your language, and I can talk you through it right now in Spanish if that's easier.
column9: Form states it is available in another language or accessible format. Substitute the patient's actual language.

column4: Do I fill in the whole thing?
column5: Do I answer everything again? · It's already filled in
column6: No. Just check what's printed and only write in things that changed. If everything is right, you tick the box and sign.
column9: The confirm-or-correct model, said plainly. This is the answer that most shortens the perceived task.

column4: Whose name is on this as my worker?
column5: Who is handling my case?
column6: [Read worker name and county phone number from the case record.]
column9: Pre-populated on the form. If Mvue does not hold it, Maya says she will find out.

column4: I didn't get the packet but the address you have is right
column5: The address you have is correct but nothing came · You have the right address but no letter arrived · My address is right, but I never got anything · Correct address but I didn't receive the packet
column6: That does happen sometimes even when the address is right. Let me confirm the address on file with you — if it's correct I'll flag it with the county so someone can look into why the packet didn't reach you, and if it needs updating we'll take the new one and have the county update your file and get back to you.
column9: Two-step: (1) confirm address on file; (2a) address correct ? flag with county for re-send; (2b) address wrong ? collect new address (defer to S4 no-packet path), county updates and gets back. Never claim Maya has updated the county record.

column4: When is this due?
column5: How long do I have? · What's the last day?
column6: [Read the due date from the case record.] If it's not on record: I want to give you the exact date rather than guess — let me confirm it and come back to you.
column9: THE canonical T2 field. Never inferred from the notice date, never estimated, never rounded.

column4: What if I'm late?
column5: I missed the date · Is it too late?
column6: It may still be fixable. Don't assume it's over — let me get you to someone who can check where your case stands.
column9: Deliberately non-committal. The cure-period rules are real but the specifics are UNVERIFIED and case-dependent. Do not name a number of days.

column4: How long do I have to fix it after my coverage stopped?
column5: Can I still get it back? · How many months do I have?
column6: There is a window after coverage stops, and I don't want to give you the wrong number. Let me get you to a specialist who can look at your case.
column9: Cure-period length must be confirmed with DHCS or the county before any spoken figure is approved.

column4: How long does it take once I send it?
column5: When will I hear back? · How fast is it?
column6: For Medi-Cal the county has up to forty-five days to decide, though it's often quicker.
column9: 45 days is stated for Medi-Cal and cash aid; 30 days is CalFresh. Do not mix them

column4: How soon do I have to report changes later?
column5: If something changes do I have to tell you?
column6: Yes — tell the county within ten days if anything changes, like your address, your income, or who lives with you.
column9: Ten days for Medi-Cal. Thirty days if they are insured through Covered California — a separate clock.

column4: The county asked me for something and I don't know what.
column5: I got another letter · They want more papers
column6: [Read the outstanding county request from the case record.] If not held: let me find out exactly what they're asking for so you only have to do it […] [cell clipped in photo]
column9: Guessing here makes the patient send the wrong document and restarts the clock.

column4: Can I get help with bills from before I applied?
column5: I have a bill from two months ago
column6: Sometimes yes — Medi-Cal can look at bills from the three months before you apply. Let me flag that so it gets asked.
column9: Retroactive coverage. Real revenue for the clinic and rarely raised by patients

column1: CONTACT INFORMATION AND ADDRESS — MC 216 page 2

column4: I moved. What do I do?
column5: I have a new address · I don't live there
column6: That's important — a lot of people lose coverage just because letters go […] [row clipped in photo]
column9: Maya cannot update the county record.

column4: I don't have an address.
column5: I'm staying with people · I'm not housed right now
column6: That's okay, and it doesn't stop you. You can use a mailing address that's different from where you sleep, and we can help you sort one out.

column4: Which phone number should I give?
column5: I have two phones · Should I put my work number?
column6: Give whichever number reaches you most reliably. You can list more than one.

column4: Do I have to give an email?
column5: I don't have email · Do you need my email?
column6: No, email is optional. You don't need one.

column4: Can you write to me in my language?
column5: Can you send it in Spanish? · I read better in Chinese
column6: Yes. You can tell them which language to write to you in and which to speak to you in — they can be different.

column4: How do you already have my information?
column5: Where did you get this? · Who gave you my details?
column6: The county already has your file, so most of the form comes pre-printed. I'm calling from [clinic name], where you get your care.

column4: Can I choose how you contact me?
column5: Stop calling, just mail it · I'd rather text
column6: Yes. You can say whether you'd rather be contacted by phone, mail, or email, and we'll follow that.

column4: Am I deaf-accessible / can I get large print?
column5: I can't hear well on the phone · I need big print
column6: Yes — you can get this in large print, audio, or other formats, and there's free help for that.

column4: Can I use the clinic as my mailing address?
column5: Can you get my mail? · Can it come to the clinic?
column6: That may be possible and it's worth asking. Let me get you to someone who can set it up properly.

column1: GETTING HELP AND WHO CAN ACT FOR YOU

column4: Can someone help me fill this in?
column5: I don't understand it · Can you do it for me?
column6: Yes, and it's free. There are certified counsellors at [clinic name] who do this every day, in your language.

column4: Can someone else deal with this for me?
column5: Can my daughter handle it? · I want my son to talk to them
column6: Yes. You can name someone — a family member, friend, carer, or an advocate — to help with your Medi-Cal and speak to the county for you.

column4: Can you submit it for me?
column5: Can you just do it? · Will you send it in?
column6: We can, if you give us permission first. It takes a few minutes and I'll read you exactly what you're agreeing to.

column4: How do I change who represents me?
column5: I don't want my ex handling it anymore
column6: You can change that at any time. Let me get you to someone who can do it properly with the county.

column4: Can I do this in person instead?
column5: I'd rather come in · I don't want to do this on the phone
column6: Of course. I can book you with a counsellor at a clinic near you who speaks your language.

column4: Is there a cost for this help?
column5: How much do you charge? · Do I have to pay you?
column6: Nothing at all. The help is free, and we will never ask you for money or a payment of any kind.

column4: Who do I have to include?
column5: Who counts as my household?
column6: Your spouse or partner, your children who live with you, any parents living with their children, and anyone on your tax return if you file one.

column4: Do I include my boyfriend or my roommate?
column5: My girlfriend lives here · What about the guy renting a room?
column6: No. A boyfriend, girlfriend, or roommate applies on their own form if they want health coverage.

column4: Someone claims me as a dependent. What do I do?
column5: My mum claims me on her taxes
column6: Then you include everyone in the household that claims you, plus any family living with you. It's worth having a counsellor check this one with you.

column4: My son moved out.
column5: My daughter went to college · Someone left the house
column6: Just tell them what changed and when. There's a place on the form for household changes in the last twelve months.

column4: I had a baby.
column5: There's a new baby · I gave birth
column6: Congratulations. Add them and they can get covered. Let me make sure that gets on the form properly.

column4: Does everyone have to live with me?
column5: My husband works out of town
column6: Not necessarily. Household members can have different addresses, and there's room on the form for that.

column4: Someone in my house wants to apply too.
column5: Can my wife get on it? · My mother needs coverage
column6: Yes. There's a section for someone in your household who isn't on Medi-Cal yet and wants to apply.

column4: Someone in my household died.
column5: My husband passed away
column6: I'm sorry. I'm not going to make you go through that on this call — let me get you to a person who can handle it with you.

column4: Someone in my household is in jail.
column5: My son is locked up · He's incarcerated
column6: That's on the form and it does affect things. Let me get you to a specialist rather than guess at it.

column4: Does it matter if my kids are covered and I'm not?
column5: Only my children have it
column6: It's common for different people in one family to be on different programmes, and children can be covered even when adults aren't.

column4: I don't file taxes. Can I still get Medi-Cal?
column5: I never do taxes · I don't work enough to file
column6: Yes. You don't have to file taxes to get health coverage. There's even a box for 'non-tax filer'.

column4: What is a primary tax filer?
column5: What does primary filer mean?
column6: It's just the first person listed on the tax return. If nobody files, there isn't one.

column4: What does head of household mean?
column5: Which box do I tick?
column6: It's a tax filing status — usually someone who's unmarried and supports a child or relative. If you're not sure, a counsellor can check your last return with you.

column4: Why do you need my tax information?
column5: What's tax got to do with my health?
column6: Medi-Cal works out household size and income partly from tax information. It's only used to decide health coverage.

column4: My tax situation changed. Does that matter?
column5: I got married · I'm filing separately now
column6: It can matter quite a bit, because it changes who counts in your household. Let me get you to a counsellor.

column4: What is that box about using my tax returns to renew automatically?
column5: It says something about renewing for five years
column6: If you say yes, the county can use your tax information to renew you automatically in future years, so you may not have to fill anything in. You can change your mind later.

column4: Will Medi-Cal cost me money at tax time?
column5: Will I owe anything? · Do I have to pay it back?
column6: Not for Medi-Cal. That repayment rule applies to Covered California subsidies, not to Medi-Cal.

column1: INCOME — MC 216 pages 6–7 [section title partly clipped: '…the highest-volume section']

column4: Do you want the amount before or after taxes?
column5: Is that my take-home? · Before deductions?
column6: Before. Put the amount before any taxes or deductions come out — the bigger number on your pay stub.

column4: I get paid every two weeks. What do I put?
column5: I'm paid biweekly · Twice a month?
column6: There's a choice for that. 'Every two weeks' and 'twice a month' are different options, so pick the one that matches your pay days.

column4: My hours change every week. What do I write?
column5: Some weeks I get nothing · It's different every month
column6: Then say your income changes month to month, and give what you expect for the whole next year. That's usually fairer than one week's pay stub.

column4: I work for cash. I don't have pay stubs.
column5: I get paid in cash · Nobody gives me a stub · Day labour
column6: That's fine and it's common. You can report it as self-employment, and a tax return or a simple profit and loss can work instead of stubs.

column4: What counts as income?
column5: Do I have to put everything?
column6: Money from a job, from working for yourself, and from things like Social Security, unemployment, or a pension.

column4: Does my child's SSI count? Does CalFresh count?
column5: Does food stamps count as income? · What about my disability cheque?
column6: Whether a particular payment counts is exactly the kind of thing I don't want to get wrong. Let me get you a specialist.

column4: I just lost my job.
column5: I got laid off · My hours got cut
column6: Then report the last date you got that pay. Losing income usually helps rather than hurts your Medi-Cal.

column4: Do I report tips?
column5: What about cash tips?
column6: Yes, tips count as part of what you earn.

column4: Do I report money my family sends me?
column5: My son helps me with rent · Someone gives me money
column6: It's worth putting down, including help with rent, food, or clothing. A counsellor can tell you how it's treated.

column4: What proof of income do I need to send?
column5: What papers do you want?
column6: Recent pay stubs, a benefit or award letter, or last year's tax return. Any one of those usually does it.

column4: My income is on here but it's wrong.
column5: That's not what I make · That number is old
column6: Then tick 'no' next to it and give the date you last got that income, and the new amount. That's exactly what the update section is for.

column4: Do I make too much for Medi-Cal?
column5: Am I over the limit? · Will I still qualify?
column6: That's the county's decision, and I don't want to guess about your coverage. Let me get you to someone who can look at your case properly.

column4: The county says my income doesn't match. Why?
column5: They say the numbers are different · They want proof of income again
column6: That's the most common reason a renewal gets held up, and it's fixable. Let me get you to a specialist who does this all day.

column4: Do I report my husband's income if he's not applying?
column5: He's not on Medi-Cal · Does his money count?
column6: His income usually still needs reporting even if he isn't applying. A counsellor can walk through it with you.

column4: Why would I tell you about my expenses?
column5: What's the point of this section?
column6: Because some expenses lower the income they count, which can help you. It's worth filling in.

column4: What kind of expenses count?
column5: Like what?
column6: Things like self-employment costs, student loan interest, retirement contributions, or alimony you pay.

column4: What proof do I need for expenses?
column5: How do I show it?
column6: A profit and loss statement or a tax return usually works.

column4: I'm self-employed. What can I deduct?
column5: Can I take off my gas and tools?
column6: There's more than one way to count self-employment costs and the right one depends on your situation. Let me get you a counsellor.

column4: Do I have to fill this part in?
column5: Can I skip it?
column6: You don't have to, but it can only help you, so it's usually worth a few minutes.

column1: OTHER COVERAGE AND MEDICARE — MC 216 pages 9, 11

column4: I have insurance from my job. Do I still qualify?
column5: I have work insurance · Can I have both?
column6: You can have Medi-Cal alongside other coverage in some cases. Just report the other plan and let the county work it out.

column4: Do I have to report my dental plan?
column5: It's only dental · What about vision?
column6: Yes — health, dental, vision, or pharmacy plans all go in that section.

column4: I have Medicare. Do I still need this?
column5: I'm on Medicare already
column6: Yes, still send it back. Many people have both, and Medi-Cal can help with Medicare costs.

column4: I don't know which parts of Medicare I have.
column5: What's Part B? · I don't know my plan
column6: You can call Medicare directly on 1-800-633-4227 and they'll tell you. Or a counsellor can help you find out.

column4: My other insurance is ending.
column5: I'm losing my work plan
column6: That's worth reporting — there's a place for coverage that ended or is ending in the last ninety days.

column4: Should I drop my other insurance?
column5: Is it better to just use Medi-Cal?
column6: I can't advise you on that one, and it matters too much to guess. Let me get you to a specialist.

column4: Someone in my family is in a nursing home.
column5: My mother is in long-term care
column6: Long-term care has its own rules and I don't want to get them wrong. Let me get you to someone who handles that.

column4: I'm pregnant.
column5: I'm expecting · I'm having a baby
column6: Congratulations — do tell them, because pregnancy can change what you're eligible for and there's extra help available.

column4: I was in foster care.
column5: I aged out of foster care
column6: That matters. If you were in foster care on or after your eighteenth birthday, in any state, you may be covered up to twenty-six.

column4: My child turned nineteen.
column5: He's not a kid anymore · She's twenty now
column6: There's a question about that — being nineteen or twenty and a full-time student is asked separately.

column4: Someone in my house has a disability.
column5: My son is autistic · I'm disabled
column6: There's a place to say that. It can open up extra help, so it's worth putting down.

column4: Can I get help with in-home care?
column5: Who helps me at home? · I need someone to help me bathe
column6: Yes, there's a programme for in-home care and you can ask for information about it right on the form.

column4: Can my kids get check-ups and dental?
column5: Do my children get a dentist?
column6: Yes — there's a no-cost programme for children under twenty-one, and you can ask for information about it on the form.

column4: Can I get help with food?
column5: Do you do food stamps? · I need groceries
column6: Yes. There's a food programme for pregnant and breastfeeding people and children under five, and CalFresh for food more generally. I can flag both.

column1: TRUST, PRIVACY AND 'WHO ARE YOU' — highest-stakes non-clinical set

column4: Who is this?
column5: Who am I speaking to? · Where are you calling from?
column6: I'm an automated assistant calling for [clinic name], where you get your care. I'm calling about your Medi-Cal renewal.

column4: Are you a robot?
column5: Am I talking to a computer? · Are you real?
column6: I'm an automated assistant, yes. If you'd rather speak to a person, I can put you through right now.

column4: How do I know this isn't a scam?
column5: I don't trust this · People try to trick me
column6: That's a fair question and I'd rather you checked. Hang up and call [clinic main line] yourself, and ask about your Medi-Cal renewal.

column4: How did you get my number?
column5: Who gave you my details?
column6: From your records at [clinic name]. I'm not calling from a company you don't know.

column4: Are you going to ask me for money?
column5: Is this going to cost me? · Do you want my card number?
column6: No. We will never ask you for money, a card number, or a bank account. If anyone ever does, it isn't us.

column4: Do you work for the government?
column5: Are you from the county? · Are you the state?
column6: No. I'm calling for [clinic name], your health centre. The county makes the decisions about your coverage.

column4: Who sees my information?
column5: Is this private? · Who do you tell?
column6: Your information is private and confidential by law, and it's used to run your health coverage.

column4: Do you have my Social Security number?
column5: Don't ask me for my social
column6: I won't ask you for it. If it's needed at all, that's handled with a person, never with me.

column4: Stop calling me.
column5: Take me off your list · Don't call again
column6: Understood, I'll take you off. Sorry to have bothered you.

column4: Can I call you back?
column5: I'm busy right now · Call me later
column6: Of course. You can reach us on [clinic line], or tell me a better time and we'll call you.

column4: Someone already called me about this and I gave them information.
column5: I think I got scammed · I gave someone my details
column6: Let me get you to a person straight away so we can work out what happened.

column1: IMMIGRATION AND ENFORCEMENT — T4, NEVER ANSWERED

column4: Will this affect my green card or my status?
column5: Public charge · Will it hurt my case? · Will it stop my papers?
column6: That's a really important question and I'm not the right one to answer it. Let me get you to a specialist right now — they do this every day and it's confidential.

column4: Will you tell immigration about me?
column5: Does ICE see this? · Will they find out?
column6: I understand why you're asking. I want you to hear that from a person rather than from me — let me put you through now.

column4: Can I apply if I don't have papers?
column5: I'm undocumented · I don't have status
column6: Let me get you to a specialist who can answer that properly and confidentially.

column4: My kids are citizens but I'm not.
column5: Only my children have status
column6: That comes up a lot and there is help for it. Let me get you to someone who can go through it with you.

column4: My status changed this year. What do I put?
column5: I got my green card · I have a new document number
column6: There is a question about that on the form, and I want a person to help you with it. Let me put you through.

column4: Is it safe for me to fill this in?
column5: Should I even do this? · Is it risky?
